title: Jetstar Flight Returns to Brisbane After Medical Emergency
text: Jetstar Flight Returns to Brisbane After Medical Emergency Jetstar flight JQ9 departed Brisbane Airport but returned about 90 minutes after takeoff when a passenger collapsed and lost consciousness. Cabin crew called for medical assistance and the aircraft dumped fuel for about 20 minutes before landing. Paramedics and airport staff boarded to remove the passenger on a stretcher. The incident caused significant delays, leaving passengers waiting on the tarmac for at least another hour after landing and pushing back travel plans by around six hours. Flight JQ9 departed Brisbane Airport about 10.50am AEST on Friday but was diverted back after a passenger reportedly collapsed and lost consciousness. Another passenger on board, who asked not to be named, told 7NEWS.com.au the emergency unfolded about 90 minutes into the flight, when cabin crew called for medical professionals to assist. “Over speakers they asked for medical staff like doctors or nurses. Someone has collapsed unconscious at the back of the plane,” she said. The witness said crew rushed through the aisles carrying medical kits, while about 20 people gathered at the back of the aircraft. She said the aircraft dumped fuel for about 20 minutes before returning to Brisbane, where emergency services were waiting.“When we landed, about five paramedics came on board and about five airport staff and border security,” she said. “They put the person on a stretcher tarp thing and two staff members dragged the person out along the aisle. ”Be the first to know:But the disruption continued after the aircraft landed, with passengers left waiting on board.The witness said the plane had been sitting on the tarmac for about an hour as of 1.30pm AEST, with the pilot warning it would be at least another 45 minutes before departure. She criticised Jetstar’s handling of the incident, saying the diversion had significantly disrupted travel plans.“It has massively inconvenienced me and everyone else on board. Our travel will be delayed by at least 6 hours,” she said. She said the delay could leave travellers struggling to find transport from Tokyo’s Narita Airport late at night, while some could lose a night’s accommodation. It is not yet known what caused the medical emergency or the condition of the affected passenger.Jetstar confirmed a passenger experienced a medical episode on board the flight.“The safety and wellbeing of our customers and crew is our number one priority,” a spokesperson for the airline said. “We thank customers for their patience and understanding while our crew attended to a medical incident on board the flight. ”

Flight JQ9 departed Brisbane Airport about 10.50am AEST on Friday but was diverted back after a passenger reportedly collapsed and lost consciousness. Another passenger on board, who asked not to be named, told 7NEWS.com.au the emergency unfolded about 90 minutes into the flight, when cabin crew called for medical professionals to assist. The witness said crew rushed through the aisles carrying medical kits, while about 20 people gathered at the back of the aircraft.
